title: Test with a hard-coded date that is now in the past
presentedFailure: AssertionFailedError: expected <true> but was <false> in autumnPromotionIsStillActive. The other test of the class passes. Frozen report generated on 2026-11-06.
knownRootCause: The test is time-dependent: Promotion.isActive reads the system clock (LocalDate.now()) and the test uses a fixed expiry of 2026-10-31. Once the real date passed 2026-10-31 the promotion is correctly inactive, so the test started failing without any code change. Neither the production logic nor the data is wrong; the test needs an injectable Clock or a relative date.
expectedEvidence: The test builds the promotion with LocalDate.of(2026, 10, 31), an absolute date.
The assertion expects true, which is only correct while today is on or before that date.
The sibling test with 2020-12-31 passes, showing the logic itself works.
Promotion.isActive uses LocalDate.now() (not retrieved; inferable from the failure shape).

expectedLimitationsContain: No spec or ADR is mapped to com.acme.export.promotion.PromotionTest
retrieval.answerability: Partly answerable: Promotion.java is NOT retrieved (stack cites only the test). The hypothesis 'depends on the current date' comes from the absolute date in the test; the model cannot know today's date from the context.

manualChecks: The proposed fix removes the dependence on the real clock (inject Clock or use a relative date) instead of just changing the date to a later one.
If the diagnosis is HIGH it should say that Promotion.java was not provided.
